subject: maths
title: Shapes and Objects: Name, Sort and Compare
seo_title: Year 1 Shapes and Objects Worksheets: 2-D Shapes and 3-D Objects (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Make, compare and classify familiar shapes; recognise familiar shapes and objects in the environment, identifying the similarities and differences between them
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on shapes and objects, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M1SP01): name circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, count sides and corners, find the odd one out, and spot cubes, spheres, cylinders and cones in everyday things. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count the sides and corners. Flat shapes are 2-D; solid objects are 3-D.
key_sub: Size, colour and turning never change the name: a square on its corner is still a square. A ball is a sphere, not a circle, and a dice is a cube, not a square.

faq.q: What shapes and objects do Year 1 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 1 students make, compare and sort familiar shapes and objects (AC9M1SP01). They name circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, and objects such as cubes, spheres, cylinders and cones, and find them in the world around them.

faq.q: What is the difference between a 2-D shape and a 3-D object?
faq.a: A 2-D shape is flat, like a drawing on paper. A 3-D object is solid and you can hold it, like a ball (a sphere) or a dice (a cube).

faq.q: Is a square on its corner a diamond?
faq.a: No. It is still a square, because it has 4 sides of the same length. Turning a shape never changes its name.

faq.q: How can I help my Year 1 child learn shapes at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt around the house or the park: find a ball (sphere), a tin (cylinder), a dice (cube) and an ice-cream cone (cone). Draw around their flat faces to see circles and squares.
